findings.claim: Non-atomic two-phase persistence makes classification unrecoverable after partial failure: the INSERT commits in session 1 before classification/scoring, and the update commits in session 2. If session 2 raises (transient DB error) or the worker dies between the commits (task_acks_late=True redelivery), the retried task hits the dedup short-circuit and returns status 'duplicate' WITHOUT re-running classification or scoring. The Lead stays permanently at status='Nuevo', qualification_score=0, conversacion_history=NULL; the task reports success ('duplicate'), so no DLQ entry and no 'failed' status is ever emitted. This silently violates REQ-DM-LEAD-04 (classification persisted) and REQ-DM-LEAD-03 (score/status) for the affected lead.
proof_refs: agency/workers/lead_persist_task.py:178 — first await session.commit() inside the dedup-check block, before classification
agency/workers/lead_persist_task.py:191-197 — second session: session.get + update + commit (only failure point after guaranteed INSERT)
agency/workers/lead_persist_task.py:151-160 — duplicate branch returns early; retry re-entry never re-classifies
agency/workers/lead_persist_task.py:224-228 — retry/DLQ only on exception; a 'duplicate' return is success, so no DLQ write
agency/workers/celery_app.py:34 — task_acks_late=True makes mid-task worker loss trigger redelivery into the duplicate path
agency/tests/unit/test_lead_persist_task.py:220-261 — DLQ test patches persist_lead_core wholesale; no test covers retry-after-partial-insert

findings.claim: dedup_hash is scoped to (ig_user_id, message) only, not tenant, and the column is UNIQUE at the DB level. The same IG user sending identical text to two different accounts mapped to different tenants makes the second tenant's webhook return the FIRST tenant's lead_id as 'duplicate', so the second tenant never receives its own Lead row; the dedup lookup also queries globally (no tenant filter). REQ-DM-LEAD-01's resolved-tenant contract is therefore violated for the second tenant in this scenario, and the duplicate response leaks another tenant's lead_id into the second flow. Tests only exercise same-tenant duplicates.
proof_refs: agency/workers/lead_persist_task.py:148-160 — SELECT Lead WHERE dedup_hash == dedup, no tenant predicate; returns existing.id
agency/backend/db/models.py:152 — dedup_hash unique=True enforces cross-tenant uniqueness
agency/tests/unit/test_lead_persist_task.py:99-126 — dedup test uses one tenant only

findings.claim: REQ-DM-LEAD-06's 'no Graph API messaging call is made' clause is not actually asserted. The test wraps the real node_send_dm_reply with AsyncMock(wraps=...), so the real node executes; assertions only check await_count==1 and absence of the string 'pending_manual' in result/history. Any future real Graph API call added inside the send node or graph path would still pass this test (the wrapped function runs any real network code for real). The test name and docstring overclaim what they verify; today there is no defect (dm_graph.py only logs + emits SSE).
proof_refs: agency/tests/unit/test_lead_persist_task.py:193-198 — AsyncMock(wraps=node_send_dm_reply) executes the real node; only await_count and 'pending_manual' string absence asserted
openspec/changes/5-value-leaps/spec.md:57-63 — REQ-DM-LEAD-06 requires 'no Graph API messaging call is made and no simulated pending_manual state'

findings.claim: The dm_graph invocation (graph.ainvoke) has no timeout or upper bound, and in production it performs a real LLM call (with Redis budget guard), a Qdrant query, and SSE emissions per persisted lead. A hung LLM/Qdrant call blocks the Celery task indefinitely: the message is not acked (task_acks_late=True) and the shared 'webhooks' queue (also used by webhook_dlq_task, concurrency=1 in dev) stalls. If the worker is then killed, redelivery lands in the dedup short-circuit and produces the permanent half-persisted state described in RELIABILITY-001. The documented 'best-effort, never breaks persistence' guarantee (module docstring) covers exceptions but not hangs.
proof_refs: agency/workers/lead_persist_task.py:95 — bare await graph.ainvoke, no asyncio.wait_for or timeout
agency/workers/celery_app.py:34 — task_acks_late=True (unacked message blocks delivery on kill)
agency/workers/celery_app.py:39 — workers.lead_persist_task.* and workers.webhook_dlq_task.* share queue 'webhooks'
agency/workers/celery_app.py:28-35 — no per-task soft/hard time limits configured

findings.claim: conversacion_history is overwritten with a single-entry list (json.dumps([history_entry])) instead of appending, so any future re-classification of the same lead (e.g., a retry path that re-runs classification or a later enhancement) would silently erase prior history entries. Harmless in the current single-shot flow (duplicates short-circuit before classification), but the column is named and typed as history.
proof_refs: agency/workers/lead_persist_task.py:74-82 — _read_intent reads history[-1], consistent with single-entry writes only
